questions.q: What is the DOM in a browser?
o: A stored copy of every HTML file on the server
A live in-memory tree of the page after HTML is parsed
A JavaScript library that builds single-page apps
A network protocol that ships HTML to the browser
questions.x: When the browser gets HTML, a parser builds a tree of elements, attributes, and text nodes in memory. Scripts read and change that live tree. What you see on screen is backed by it, not by the original file sitting still on disk.
questions.h: The DOM is what the browser builds after it reads tags. Is that a static file, or a live structure scripts can change?

questions.q: A script changes a node's textContent. What happens if the user reloads the page?
o: The edit is written back into the original HTML file on disk
The browser parses the original HTML again and the edit is gone
The browser stores that edit in localStorage automatically
The server is sent a PATCH request carrying the new text
questions.x: DOM edits live only in browser memory for that page load. A reload fetches and parses the original HTML again, so the paragraph goes back to whatever the server sent.
questions.h: The DOM is live in memory for one page load. What does the browser start from when it loads the page again?

questions.q: Consider these claims about the DOM. (1) The first HTML from the server is only a starting point. (2) Scripts can add, remove, or change nodes after that. (3) A reload writes DOM edits back to the HTML file. Which option is correct?
o: Only the first claim is true
Only the first two claims are true
Only the third claim is true
All of these statements are true
questions.x: Claims 1 and 2 are true. The server HTML is only the starting tree, and scripts can change nodes later. Claim 3 is false: a reload re-parses the original HTML and drops in-memory edits. All is wrong because claim 3 is false.
questions.h: DOM edits live in memory for one page load. What does a reload start from, the live tree or the original HTML?

questions.q: Why does assigning a string to innerHTML run the HTML parser again?
o: innerHTML encrypts the string before it is shown
The browser parses that string into new DOM nodes
innerHTML posts the string to the server first
innerHTML only accepts markup that is already sanitized
questions.x: innerHTML is not plain text. The parser reads tags, attributes, and quotes in the string and builds new nodes. That is why untrusted data in an innerHTML assignment can change the resulting tree.
questions.h: innerHTML does not print the string literally. What does the browser do with angle brackets inside it?

questions.q: In a div#comments that contains a p tag, what does document.querySelector('#comments p') return?
o: The raw HTML string from the server response
The p element node inside that div in the live tree
A CSS stylesheet rule that matches the selector
The HTTP headers from the original page request
questions.x: querySelector walks the live DOM and returns the first matching element node. Here that is the p inside the comments div, which JavaScript can then read or change.
questions.h: querySelector searches the in-memory tree. What kind of object does it return on a match?
